distillation_scope.disease_name_scope: Pure disease-name distillation. No genotype, transmission route, pregnancy, chronicity, severity, complication, or mimic qualifier was added to the disease name.
distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer disease leaf for acute HEV infection. Pregnancy-associated fulminant course, immunosuppression-associated persistence, extrahepatic neurologic/renal/pancreatic complications, and acute liver failure are represented as mechanisms, axes, event hazards, risk factors, or treatment modifiers.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Acquisition of hepatitis E virus through contaminated water/food, zoonotic meat exposure, transfusion, or vertical/perinatal context followed by enteric amplification, viremia, hepatocyte infection, biliary excretion, and stool shedding.
Innate antiviral and inflammatory response producing fever, malaise, fatigue, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, and early systemic symptoms.
Antiviral immune injury to infected hepatocytes causing abrupt ALT/AST elevation, hepatic tenderness, jaundice, and usually self-limited recovery in immunocompetent hosts.
Hepatocellular and canalicular dysfunction causing direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia, dark urine, jaundice, pruritus, and mild-to-moderate cholestatic enzyme elevation.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Synthetic failure and acute liver failure transition
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Severe hepatocyte dysfunction with impaired clotting-factor synthesis, glucose/ammonia handling failure, hepatic encephalopathy, cerebral edema, bleeding vulnerability, shock, and transplant-level deterioration.

Pregnancy, especially late pregnancy in endemic genotype 1/2 contexts, alters immune and hormonal signaling and reduces maternal-fetal reserve, increasing fulminant hepatitis, coagulopathy, shock, fetal demise, and death hazards.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Extrahepatic immune neurologic and renal activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Immune-mediated or direct extrahepatic activity causing Guillain-Barre syndrome, peripheral neuropathy, neuralgic amyotrophy, meningoencephalitic findings, glomerular/renal injury, pancreatitis, cytopenias, and respiratory failure through neurologic weakness.

Failure to clear HEV in solid-organ transplant, hematologic malignancy, HIV, chemotherapy, biologic, or high-dose steroid contexts, causing persistent viremia, chronic hepatitis, fibrosis progression, relapse after treatment, and altered serologic sensitivity.
Effective immune control and hepatocyte regeneration causing HEV RNA decline, IgG maturation, falling aminotransferases and bilirubin, synthetic recovery, and decreasing event hazards.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Compatible waterborne, foodborne, zoonotic, transfusion, or outbreak context raises the prior probability of acute HEV.
Fecal-oral exposure is a major HEV acquisition route.
Acute HEV induces anti-HEV IgM during symptomatic illness.
IgG appears during or after acute HEV and can persist.
Serum/plasma HEV RNA confirms active infection and is important when serology is blunted.
HEV viral load quantifies active replication.
HEV is shed in stool and can persist longer than serum RNA.
Viral infection drives systemic prodromal symptoms.
Hepatotropic replication provides antigenic substrate for immune hepatocyte injury.
Fever may occur during acute HEV prodrome.
Malaise, fatigue, and lethargy are common in acute viral hepatitis.
Loss of appetite is common in symptomatic acute HEV.
Nausea and vomiting can dominate presentation.
Epigastric or right upper quadrant discomfort can occur with hepatic inflammation.
ALT rises with HEV hepatocellular injury and may reach the thousands.
AST rises with acute hepatocyte injury.
LDH can rise with severe hepatocellular injury or extrahepatic tissue injury.
Hepatic inflammation can produce RUQ tenderness.
Hepatocellular inflammation impairs bilirubin handling and bile excretion.
Acute HEV frequently causes hyperbilirubinemia.
Hepatocellular cholestasis often produces direct-predominant bilirubin elevation.
Visible jaundice follows bilirubin accumulation.
Conjugated bilirubinuria causes dark urine.
Cholestasis can cause itching.
ALP may rise variably in acute HEV.
GGT can rise with cholestatic or hepatocellular injury.
Hepatic synthetic failure prolongs INR.
Severe acute liver injury can impair glucose homeostasis.
Severe liver failure impairs ammonia handling.
Hyperammonemia and liver failure produce encephalopathy.
HEV ALF can progress from confusion to coma.
Coagulopathy plus encephalopathy is the critical ALF pathway.
Coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, procedures, and DIC overlap increase bleeding hazard.
ALF, dehydration, shock, and immune renal injury can produce AKI.
Pregnancy activates the pregnancy-specific severity-modulation pathway.
Pregnancy-associated immune-hormonal context can amplify HEV liver failure.
Maternal HEV ALF, shock, coagulopathy, and placental/fetal stress increase fetal loss hazard.
HEV can be associated with peripheral neuropathic manifestations.
HEV-associated Guillain-Barre syndrome can present with rapidly progressive symmetric weakness.
GBS often produces hyporeflexia or areflexia.
HEV is a recognized trigger of GBS.
Severe GBS can involve respiratory muscles and bulbar function.
Cellular immune impairment reduces HEV clearance and can blunt serology.
Persistent replication maintains measurable HEV RNA.
Persistent viremia beyond the acute window can transition to chronic HEV in immunocompromised hosts.
Successful immune clearance lowers viral load.
Hepatocellular injury resolves during recovery.
Synthetic function improves as hepatocytes recover.
HEV-related ALF is the dominant lethal pathway.
Respiratory failure from GBS, ALF, aspiration, or sepsis increases death hazard.
AKI worsens metabolic, volume, and ICU reserve in severe HEV.
Pregnancy-associated HEV has increased maternal mortality when ALF develops.

axes.shape_free_text: Days from first compatible systemic, gastrointestinal, neurologic, dark urine, or jaundice symptom to current observation.

Compatible HEV acquisition context: contaminated water or food, poor sanitation, outbreak, travel/endemic setting, pork or wild game exposure, transfusion, occupational animal exposure, or pregnancy/vertical context.
Untreated water, poor sanitation, contaminated food, outbreak, or travel/endemic exposure consistent with HEV.
Undercooked pork, pig offal, wild boar, deer, or related zoonotic HEV exposure.
Anti-HEV IgM positivity supporting acute or recent HEV infection.
Anti-HEV IgG positivity reflecting recent or prior exposure; supports acute disease only with IgM/RNA or compatible course.
HEV RNA detected in serum, plasma, or blood.
Quantitative HEV RNA viral load in serum, plasma, or blood.
HEV RNA detected in stool during acute infection, prolonged shedding, or treatment monitoring.
Current pregnancy or immediate postpartum context relevant to HEV severity and maternal-fetal risk.
Gestational age when acute HEV is observed; late pregnancy increases severity context.
Solid organ transplant immunosuppression, hematologic malignancy, chemotherapy, biologics, advanced HIV, high-dose steroids, or other impaired cellular immunity affecting HEV clearance.
Reported or documented fever during acute HEV prodrome or severe course.
Measured body temperature.
Heart rate reflecting fever, dehydration, pain, shock, pregnancy physiology, respiratory failure, or ICU complications.
Respiratory rate; rises with dyspnea, shock, pregnancy, acidosis, GBS respiratory weakness, or ventilatory failure.
Pulse oximetry oxygen saturation, reduced by respiratory failure, pneumonia, aspiration, shock, or severe GBS.
Systolic blood pressure; usually preserved in uncomplicated HEV and falls with shock, sepsis, bleeding, dehydration, or ALF.
Mean arterial pressure derived from blood pressure and perfusion state.
Malaise, fatigue, lethargy, asthenia, or low energy during acute HEV.
Loss of appetite or poor oral intake.
Nausea, vomiting, emesis, or inability to tolerate oral intake.
Epigastric, right upper quadrant, or diffuse abdominal discomfort from acute hepatitis or overlap biliary/pancreatic context.
Epigastric pain or tenderness during acute HEV.
Right upper quadrant pain or tenderness from liver capsule, gallbladder edema, or biliary mimic context.
Visible jaundice or scleral icterus due to bilirubin accumulation.
Dark, brown, or tea-colored urine from bilirubinuria.
Itching from cholestasis or high bile-acid/bilirubin burden.
Tender liver edge or right upper quadrant tenderness.
Palpable or imaged hepatomegaly during acute hepatitis or ALF.
Confusion, disorientation, reduced alertness, coma, seizure-related alteration, or encephalopathy in severe HEV/ALF.
West Haven or clinically equivalent hepatic encephalopathy grade.
GCS score; decreases with severe encephalopathy, intubation, sedation, shock, or cerebral edema.
Peripheral sensory or motor neuropathy associated with HEV extrahepatic immune activity.
Symmetric limb weakness progressing from lower limbs upward, compatible with GBS phenotype.
Areflexia or hyporeflexia in the setting of suspected GBS.
High CSF protein with normal or near-normal leukocyte count, supporting GBS when present.
EMG/nerve-conduction evidence of demyelinating polyneuropathy in HEV-associated GBS context.
AST rises with acute HEV hepatocellular injury; may be hundreds to thousands.
ALT rises with acute HEV hepatocellular injury; often exceeds AST and may reach the thousands.
LDH can rise with severe hepatocellular injury, extrahepatic tissue injury, hemolysis, or critical illness.
Total bilirubin during acute HEV; can be modest, marked, or extreme in severe cholestatic/ALF presentations.
Direct bilirubin fraction from hepatocellular cholestasis.
ALP is usually normal to moderately elevated in acute HEV; high values raise cholestatic or biliary mimic context.
GGT can rise with cholestatic or hepatocellular injury and may remain elevated during recovery.
INR rises with acute hepatic synthetic dysfunction; INR elevation plus encephalopathy activates ALF hazard.
Measured PT in seconds when INR is reported or unavailable.
Albumin may be normal in acute HEV, lower with pregnancy dilution, inflammation, chronic liver disease, prolonged hepatitis, or critical illness.
Ammonia rises with detoxification failure in severe HEV ALF.
Glucose may fall with severe ALF or poor intake and may rise with stress or dextrose treatment.
Hemoglobin reflects baseline reserve, bleeding, hemolysis, pregnancy dilution, procedures, ICU course, or ribavirin toxicity context.
WBC can be normal, low with viral illness, or high with stress, pregnancy, sepsis, or ICU infection.
Platelets may be normal in uncomplicated HEV and low with pregnancy severe illness, DIC, sepsis, hypersplenism, or immune complications.
Creatinine rises with AKI from dehydration, shock, ALF, immune renal disease, pregnancy complications, or nephrotoxins.
BUN rises with dehydration, renal dysfunction, bleeding, catabolism, or AKI.
Sodium can fall with vomiting, ALF, pregnancy, renal dysfunction, or ICU fluids.
Potassium varies with vomiting, renal dysfunction, acidosis, dialysis, or critical illness.
Bicarbonate reflects vomiting, acidosis, renal dysfunction, shock, or ventilation context.
Hazard of acute liver failure with coagulopathy, encephalopathy, hypoglycemia, hyperammonemia, shock, cerebral edema, or transplant-level deterioration during HEV.
Hazard of hepatic encephalopathy during severe HEV liver failure.
Hazard of cerebral edema or intracranial hypertension in HEV acute liver failure.
AKI hazard from severe HEV, dehydration, shock, renal immune injury, pregnancy critical illness, or ICU complications.
Major bleeding hazard from coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, pregnancy/delivery, procedures, DIC, or ICU complications.
Hazard of HEV-associated Guillain-Barre syndrome or acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
Respiratory failure hazard from HEV-associated GBS, ALF encephalopathy, aspiration, pneumonia, sepsis, or shock.
Need for intubation or mechanical ventilation due to GBS respiratory muscle weakness, ALF coma/airway risk, sepsis, or hypoxemia.
Fetal demise hazard in maternal HEV illness, especially when maternal ALF, shock, coagulopathy, hypoxemia, or severe systemic illness occurs.
Hazard that active HEV replication persists beyond the acute episode and evolves into chronic hepatitis, mainly in immunocompromised hosts.
Context limiting ribavirin use, including pregnancy, severe anemia, intolerance, advanced renal dysfunction, or high fetal toxicity concern.
Feasibility of reducing immunosuppression without unacceptable graft rejection, malignancy, autoimmune, or transplant risk.
Availability and feasibility of intubation, mechanical ventilation, and ICU airway monitoring.
System feasibility and candidacy context for urgent liver transplant evaluation or rescue transfer in HEV acute liver failure.

Lifespan-only mortality hazard emerging from HEV acute liver failure, pregnancy-associated fulminant disease, cerebral edema, shock, respiratory failure, AKI, bleeding, sepsis, or failed rescue pathway.

Hyperammonemia contributes to encephalopathy.

Creatinine rise reflects AKI severity.
Pregnancy, especially late pregnancy in endemic contexts, raises HEV fulminant-course hazard.
Maternal ALF, shock, coagulopathy, and hypoxemia can precipitate fetal demise.
Peripheral neuropathy and ascending weakness co-occur in GBS presentations.
Rapidly progressive symmetric weakness raises GBS event probability.
GBS can progress to respiratory failure requiring ventilation.
Impaired cellular immunity increases persistent HEV replication.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: General ward-level support is insufficient once ALF physiology is active.
Pregnancy lowers threshold for fetal and maternal monitoring.

treatments.context_specific_role: Maintains perfusion, nutrition, glucose, and symptom control while HEV resolves or declares severe physiology.
Reduces avoidable hepatic stress during acute HEV recovery.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Vitamin K cannot reverse INR caused by true hepatic synthetic collapse.
Cholestasis and poor intake can produce a vitamin K-responsive component.

treatments.context_specific_role: Treats a deficiency component of coagulopathy while preserving ALF evaluation.
Adjunctive liver support when HEV approaches severe acute liver injury or ALF physiology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: High-grade encephalopathy activates airway, cerebral edema, ammonia, glucose, sodium, and ICU monitoring interventions.

treatments.context_specific_role: Stabilizes ALF physiology while native recovery, delivery/obstetric decisions, transplant path, or bridge therapies are evaluated.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Pregnancy, severe anemia, or renal constraints can prevent ribavirin use.
Ribavirin has fetal toxicity and should not be treated as a routine pregnancy intervention.
Antiviral viral-load suppression matters most with persistent HEV replication.

treatments.context_specific_role: Suppresses HEV replication in persistent or selected severe non-pregnant contexts through viral-load axes rather than a semantic treatment label.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Graft rejection, malignancy, or autoimmune risk can limit reduction.
Persistent HEV RNA makes host-clearance restoration more outcome-relevant.

treatments.context_specific_role: Restores HEV clearance pressure in transplant or immunosuppressed hosts when feasible.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit depends on candidacy, center access, timing, donor availability, and control of sepsis or neurologic injury.
AKI raises urgency and peri-rescue risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue pathway for HEV acute liver failure with poor-prognosis physiology.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Immunotherapy does not immediately replace ventilatory support when weakness is advanced.

treatments.context_specific_role: Controls HEV-triggered immune neuropathy and reduces respiratory-risk trajectory through the neurologic event chain.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Ventilatory support requires equipment, airway skill, and ICU monitoring.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supports severe GBS respiratory weakness or ALF airway-risk physiology while the causal process is treated.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises acute HEV prior among acute jaundice illnesses, especially in endemic or outbreak settings.
Raises HEV prior in industrialized or sporadic cases where waterborne exposure is absent.
Amplifies fulminant hepatitis, coagulopathy, shock, fetal-demise, and maternal mortality hazards.

treatment_effect_modulation.clinical_rationale: Pregnancy creates fetal-toxicity context for ribavirin.
Pregnancy lowers the threshold for ICU and obstetric coordination.

present.trajectory_modulation: Blunts serologic response, prolongs viremia, and raises chronic HEV persistence/fibrosis pressure.

treatment_effect_modulation.clinical_rationale: Host-clearance restoration can be causal when persistence is immune-driven.
Persistent HEV RNA makes antiviral suppression outcome-relevant.

present.trajectory_modulation: Reduces hepatic reserve and raises risk from otherwise self-limited HEV hepatocellular injury.
Raises vulnerability to symptomatic disease, renal complications, respiratory failure consequences, and slower recovery.
Signals transition from uncomplicated acute hepatitis to ALF event chain.
Does not replace HEV microbiology, but once HEV is present it shifts outcome risk through GBS and respiratory event chains.

treatment_effect_modulation.clinical_rationale: Rapid GBS progression makes neurologic immunotherapy outcome-relevant.
Respiratory weakness requires monitoring and support independent of liver enzyme recovery.

present.trajectory_modulation: Amplifies tachycardia, hypotension, AKI hazard, and hospitalization need.

supportive_care: Structure acute HEV around compatible exposure, prodrome, jaundice/dark urine, hepatocellular transaminitis, bilirubin pattern, and HEV IgM or RNA evidence.
Trend AST, ALT, bilirubin fractions, ALP/GGT, INR/PT, glucose, ammonia, albumin, creatinine/BUN, platelets, mental status, and urine output rather than relying on a single snapshot.
Use HEV RNA when serology is negative or unreliable, especially in immunosuppressed patients, early infection, relapse, or chronicity monitoring.

In pregnancy, preserve gestational age, fetal status, thrombocytopenia/coagulopathy, shock, hypoxemia, and ICU/obstetric interventions as structured evidence without turning pregnancy into a separate disease name.

When INR rises, encephalopathy appears, glucose falls, ammonia rises, shock develops, respiratory status worsens, creatinine rises, or bleeding occurs, treat acute liver failure as an event chain and involve hepatology/critical care/transplant pathways early.
In immunosuppressed hosts, monitor persistent HEV RNA and chronic hepatitis/fibrosis risk; do not rely on IgM alone.

For neurologic presentations, preserve peripheral neuropathy, ascending weakness, areflexia, CSF albuminocytologic dissociation, electrodiagnostics, respiratory failure, and IVIg/plasma exchange/ventilation course as extrahepatic HEV evidence.
Avoid alcohol, unnecessary hepatotoxic drugs, dehydration, NSAID-heavy self-treatment when coagulopathic, and unsafe food/water exposures during recovery.
Ribavirin, immunosuppression reduction, ICU support, transplant evaluation, and neurologic immunotherapy should compete through context axes and outcome simulation rather than semantic labels.

Separate Acute hepatitis E from Acute liver failure as disease versus event: HEV is the disease manifold; ALF, GBS, fetal demise, chronicity, AKI, respiratory failure, and bleeding are event hazards or complications.
